title: Add a bounded torrent queue with configurable download concurrency
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Simple Torrent implements FIFO admission and activation. The current engine adds every torrent immediately and has no queue or concurrency policy. A bounded queue improves usability and protects CPU, disk, sockets and pending metadata work. Do not copy fork semantics where completed seeding handles can monopolize all downloading slots.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provide explicit queued/downloading/paused states and visible deterministic FIFO positions, with a validated configurable active-download limit and a separate bounded metadata-admission policy.
- Cap pending entries as well as active transfers; deduplicate by torrent identity. Define seeding slot behavior and manual Start capacity handling without silently bypassing limits.
- Serialize admission/completion/pause/remove/configuration transitions; release/advance each slot exactly once. Changing capacity preserves selections and does not implicitly resume user-paused torrents.
- Persist queue order and user intent using the session store. Watch imports, API additions and restoration share the same admission rules.
- With capacity two and four local fixtures, verify exactly two active downloads, advancement after pause/completion/removal, no duplicate slots, bounded metadata work, safe concurrent mutations and restart ordering.

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.
